Carrickfergus Tall Ship Project: plans to locate historic vessel Result next to Carrickfergus Castle

By Helena McManus
Published 7th Oct 2026, 16:05 BST
Updated 7th Oct 2026, 16:14 BST

A historic tall ship built in Carrickfergus more than 130 years ago could have a permanent home beside the castle as part of ambitious plans to bring the vessel back to where its story began.

Instaread

The schooner Result is the sole survivor of 38 ships designed and built by Paul Rodgers in Carrick’s shipyard between 1845 and 1893.

In 2024, volunteer-led charity and nonprofit company Result Carrickfergus Limited outlined proposals to conserve Result as part of The Carrickfergus Tall Ship Project.

The project aims to give Result a lasting place in the town as a living history attraction, education space and event venue.

In its autumn newsletter, Result Carrickfergus Limited said there was a “strong case” to include the ship in the Carrickfergus City Deal Regeneration scheme. “[This] would give the harbour a direct link to the town’s shipbuilding history,” the group added.

“Built in Carrickfergus in 1893, she could help visitors understand the maritime story behind the waterfront, while adding a distinctive attraction to the planned improvements around the harbour, castle and town centre. Her return would also give local people a visible reminder of the skills and achievements of earlier generations.

"Our proposal is not only to restore Result and return it to Carrickfergus, but also to locate it on dry land at the east end of the carpark, which would be close to her original maritime setting when it sailed to the town. This positioning, in the shadow of the castle would create a striking first impression for visitors arriving at the waterfront.

"The ship and castle would tell two connected chapters of Carrickfergus’s story in one place, giving people a clear reason to stop, explore the harbour and continue into the town centre. With parking and transport links close by, a restored Result could become an accessible landmark and a focal point for the wider regeneration scheme.”

The Carrickfergus Tall Ship Project aligns with the regeneration scheme’s aims to strengthen tourism and benefit the local community, the group believes: “Planning for her alongside the wider harbour works would allow her location, access and visitor experience to be considered as the area develops.”

About Result

Result’s long career included being requisitioned by the Royal Navy during the First World War and actively deployed as a Q-ship – seemingly harmless vessels concealing guns to lure submarines to the surface.

"Result is now the last First World War Q-ship in existence and broadening our aims not only brings a significant part of Carrickfergus’s maritime story into public view, but will also be the UK’s only monument to those who served on Q-ships,” the newsletter added.

“Our plans will also see the formation of a new Association that is contained within the company. The proposed Association would operate as part of Result Carrickfergus Limited, under the company’s board oversight. Its first programme will focus on research and publish a sourced record of Q-ships, crews, service and losses, beginning with Result; gather family stories and work with museums and archives on talks, exhibitions and school resources; hold an annual act of remembrance for Q-ship crews in Carrickfergus; build links with naval, maritime and veterans’ organisations, and develop volunteers and supporters.”

If you are interested in becoming a volunteer, e-mail: info@carrickfergustallship.com for more information.
